title: The people of the English line
dek: Twenty ancestors on Derrick's Wear and Hawkins sides, each graded on the same five-word ladder, each with what is not known.
note: Everyone here was born before 1900 and is long dead. Where a record was read the page says which; where a statement is a family tree's word, a best candidate or not proved, it says that instead, and the grade on the person is the grade of the weakest link a reader would otherwise take for granted.

people.name: Henry Robert Wear
people.why: A record was read for every step of his life from birth to burial.
people.dek: Born in Bermondsey, a fatherless boy at Watford, a printer's assistant at Letchworth, a soldier in 1914, and a machine minder who sailed for the Cape in April 1939.
facts: Birth registered at vol 1D p230. Mother's maiden name Hawkins: son of Robert Wear and Emma Hawkins.
Robert Wear, aged 31 (St Olave Southwark, vol 1D p141), about six months after his son's birth. The boy never knew him.
Aged one, with his widowed mother inside his uncle John Hawkins's household at 44 Ebury Road (RG12 piece 1120, folio 37).
Step-son of John Hull, a railway labourer, at 22 Mount Pleasant, aged 11 (RG13 piece 1312).
A boarder at 9 Ridge Road, aged 21 (RG14/7576/0009).

At the Congregational Church, Baldock. Two papers reported it and one prints him as 'Harry Ware'. He was in uniform, on furlough from Bury St Edmunds, and his battalion landed in France on 6 November.
The eldest, Leonard, has his own page. The others are not named here.
The Durban Castle, London to the Cape, occupation machine minder (transcribed 'machine minister'). Martha Maud followed on the Dunvegan Castle on 10 August with four of the children.
Aged 80. Buried at West Park Cemetery on 13 September in grave 56045, which his son Leonard bought that day (Private Graves Register, folio W 8).
gaps: His Master of the High Court estate file, MHG 10245/69, has been asked for and has not been seen.
The line from his son Leonard to Derrick rests on DNA and inference, not on a document. See the DNA page.

people.name: Martha Maud Castle
people.why: Her baptism, marriage, passage and burial are all records; only the exact birth day is a tree's word.
people.dek: The sixth of nine children, born at Baldock; she raised six children at Letchworth and sailed for Durban thirteen days before her brother died in London.
facts: Birth registered in the September quarter of 1895 at Hitchin, vol 3a p551, which agrees with a birth in July. Baptised at Baldock on 22 September 1895. The day of birth, 21 July, comes from a second-cousin match's family tree.
At the Congregational Church, Baldock. The Hertfordshire Express gives her address as Norton Street, Baldock, the first address this archive has for her.
At 72 Pix Road, in the same street as her husband's mother.
The Dunvegan Castle, London to Durban, with four of her children. Britain declared war on 3 September.

George William Castle, of 85 Jackmans-place, Letchworth, in St Bartholomew's Hospital, thirteen days after her ship sailed. He died without a will; administration went to Margaret Castle, widow, and Cyril George Castle, printer.
Aged 90. Buried in her husband's grave, 56045, at West Park.
gaps: The exact day of her birth rests on one tree; no record read here gives it.
Cyril George Castle, who shared her brother's administration, is not claimed as the brother's son.
see: The Leonard page, with the sailing and the probate

people.name: Robert Wear
people.why: His birth, marriage and death are all registered, and he is in his father's household in 1871.
people.dek: A harness-maker's youngest son from Jamaica Road, who married Emma Hawkins of Aldenham in 1881 and died eight years later, six months after his son was born.
facts: Birth registered in vol 1D. Mother's maiden name Bloom, which is the only place that name appears.
Aged 12, a scholar, in the house of his father William Wear, a harness maker, where his three older brothers worked at the same bench (RG10 piece 641, folio 40).
At St Olave, Southwark, vol 1D p455.
Louisa in 1883 at Wimbledon, Rosetta in 1886 at Bermondsey, and Henry Robert in Q3 1889 at Bermondsey.
gaps: His own occupation is not recorded in anything this archive holds; his father and his three older brothers were harness makers.
Why his first child was born at Wimbledon and the others at Bermondsey is not known.
The cause of his death is not known.

people.name: Emma Hawkins
people.why: Her baptism, both marriages' children, three censuses, the 1939 Register and her death are all records.
people.dek: Born at Aldenham, widowed at thirty-one, a stepfather's wife at St Albans, and blind in Pix Road, Letchworth, in 1939. Eighty-five years, two husbands buried, five children.
facts: Baptised there in 1859, daughter of John and Emma Hawkins. The day comes from the 1939 Register, given by Emma herself at eighty.
Aged 12, a scholar, one of six of the family's children still at home (RG10 piece 1380, folio 10).
At St Olave, Southwark. Three children follow, in 1883, 1886 and 1889.
Home to her brother's house at Watford
With her three children at 44 Ebury Road, in the household of her brother John Hawkins, a carter.

At St Albans, vol 3a p758, where the free index carries Wear Emma and Hull John on one page. He is a railway labourer; Albert is born in 1895 and Edith in 1897, both at St Albans. In 1901 she is 'Emma Hull' at 22 Mount Pleasant, St Albans (RG13 piece 1312). The certificate has not been read.

At 63 Pix Road, aged 80, widowed and incapacitated, living with her daughter Louisa and her son-in-law William Shenton. Her son Henry Robert raised his own children at 72 Pix Road, in the same street.
This archive wrote her mother's dates and history over her entry, because mother and daughter share a forename, and published the result for part of a day. Corrected.
gaps: The marriage certificate to John Hull has not been read.
When John Hull died is not established.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: George William Castle
people.why: His marriage and his death are index entries matched by name, age and district, with no certificate read. His birthplace and his parents are one researcher's tree, and the census disagrees with it.
people.dek: A farm labourer's son raised by his grandparents at Norton End after his mother died when he was under a year old.
facts: Birth registered at Hitchin. A baptism at St Mary's, Baldock, on 4 January 1863 (‘parents George & Martha, abode Willian’) comes from another researcher's tree, not from a register read here.
Martha Castle, registered at Hitchin. His father took him to her parents rather than his own.
With his grandparents at Norton End
Aged 8, 'grandson' in the house of James and Elizabeth Giddins, with his widowed father listed as their son-in-law (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).

At Hitchin, registered in the December quarter of 1882, vol 3a p567, where the free index carries both names on one page. A tree gives October, which sits inside the quarter. The certificate has not been read.
At Middle Row in 1891 and at Norton in 1901, from the same tree.
His wife told the census nine children born, eight living and one dead. The dead one is Sidney Charles, who died at two.

Aged 54, registered at Hitchin, vol 3a p607: a George W Castle, which fits a man born in Q4 1862. A search of England and Wales for a George Castle aged 54 between March 1916 and December 1917 returns this entry alone, and Hitchin has no George Castle death in 1916 at all. A match holder's own tree gave 1917 independently. The identification is by name, age and district; the certificate has not been read.
gaps: The marriage certificate has not been read. It would name both fathers, and with them Caroline's.

His death certificate has not been read, so the place and cause are not known, and the year 1917 rests on an index entry matched by name, age and district. One tree still says 1916; the index has no George Castle death at Hitchin in 1916.
The census disagrees with the tree twice: it gives his birthplace as Baldock, not Willian, and his birth year as 1863, not 1862.
see: His daughter Martha Maud, and the probate of his son

people.name: Caroline Wallis
people.born: 28 February 1862, Weston (the year from her baptism; the day and month from the 1939 Register)
people.died: 1957, registered at Hitchin as Caroline James
people.why: Her later life is documented and her marriage is an index entry. Her birth in early 1862 and her parents, Joseph Wallis and Sarah Field of Weston, rest on a baptism, two censuses and a run of Weston registers that name a Caroline Wallis and her family; no document yet joins that girl to Caroline Castle.
people.dek: She remarried in 1920 and died in 1957 as Caroline James, which is why every tree that carries her as Caroline Wallis was hunting a death registered under another surname.
facts: Baptised at Weston on 16 April 1862 as Caroline Wallis, daughter of Joseph, a labourer, and Sarah; her birth was registered at Hitchin in the March quarter of 1862 (vol 3a p230). The day and month, 28 February, come from the 1939 Register, which prints 1863; her age of 48 in the 1911 census fits 1863 and her 56 years 4 months in 1921 fits neither. The baptism, the 1871 and 1881 censuses and the 1957 death index all say 1862, so the later ages are a year or more out. The unnamed girl registered at Hitchin in March 1863 (p247) is not her.
Caroline Wallis, daughter of Joseph, a labourer, and Sarah, in the Hertfordshire baptism register at Weston. She is the only Caroline Wallis baptised there in the early 1860s.
A straw plaiter of nine, in Maiden Street

Indexed as Caroline WALLACE, nine, daughter, born at Weston, a straw plaiter, in the household of Joseph Wallace, born about 1829, and Sarah, born about 1831, with eight brothers and sisters (RG10 piece 1366, folio 41, schedule 74). The index spells the surname differently from the baptism, which is why a search on Wallis missed her.

Caroline Wallis, daughter, single, a straw plaiter, born at Weston, in the household of Joseph and Sarah Wallis with Emma, Eliza, Joseph, Sarah and George (RG11 piece 1417, folio 97, schedule 81). Eighteen months before the marriage at Hitchin in the December quarter of 1882. Her first child, Sarah Ann, was registered as a Wallis in 1882, and takes the name of the mother of this household.
At Hitchin, registered in the December quarter of 1882, vol 3a p567, with both names on the one page of the free index. A tree gives October. The certificate has not been read.
Her answer to the census question; one child, Sidney Charles, had died at two.
James James, at Hitchin (vol 3A p2077), three years after George William's death in 1917.

At 9 Boscombe Place, wife of James James, born at Weston, aged 56 years 4 months. Two children in the house are enumerated as his step-children and carry the surname Castle (RG15 piece 7079, schedule 125).
gaps: Her parents are probable and not proved. No document joins Caroline Castle to the girl baptised at Weston in April 1862; the join is the name, the parish, the date and the age, and it is strengthened by what her own children and her parents' were called. The marriage certificate of 1882 would name her father, and it is the one document that would settle it.
Her first marriage certificate has not been read. It would name her father, and ordering it is a purchase for the family to decide.
see: Her parents, Joseph Wallis and Sarah Field

people.name: Joseph Wallis
people.why: His baptism, his marriage and his death are register and index entries matched by name, parish and age; the censuses of 1851, 1871 and 1881 fit them, and no document names him as Caroline's father. His age in the censuses and at death differs by up to three years.
people.dek: A farm labourer of Weston who married the girl whose brother was lodging with him, and whose widowed mother was left with six children in 1851.
facts: William Wallis, bachelor, and Mary Foster, spinster, both of Weston, at Holy Trinity; witnesses James Watson and William Kent. Joseph is baptised five months later.
His wife is his second cousin

Joseph's father, William Wallis, was the son of Ann Phillips; Sarah's mother, Elizabeth Phillips, was the daughter of Ann's brother James. William and Elizabeth were therefore first cousins, and their children Joseph and Sarah were second cousins. The register names the brother and sister by baptism, the marriage of James Phillips and the baptisms of his children, and the link is by name, parish and the middle name of a Wallis daughter, not by a certificate.

Joseph, son of William and Mary Wallis, a labourer, at Weston Holy Trinity (FreeREG, transcribed by a volunteer from the register). He is the only Joseph Wallis baptised at Weston between 1825 and 1833. An older Joseph Wallis, baptised there in 1822 to George and Betsey, is a different man.
Married, 23, an agricultural labourer, in Weston village

With Sarah, his wife, aged 21, and James Field, a lodger of 24, all born at Weston (HO 107 piece 1709, ED 10c, folio 190, schedule 117, FreeCEN). Sarah's and James's baptisms are on her page. His widowed mother is in the same village the same night: Mary Wallis, 42, born at Wallington, a labourer's widow and a pauper, with Emma, Ann, Hesther, Eliza, Jeremiah and William and a granddaughter of one (schedule 81). Eliza, Jeremiah and William were baptised at Weston to William and Mary Wallis in 1842, 1845 and 1848; the census puts each of them a year older than the baptism does. The head of that house is a widow, so William Wallis was dead.

At Hitchin, vol 6 p711. The index names Joseph Wallis, Sarah Field, Charlotte Bigg and George Dearman on that page, which is two couples, and the Bigg and Dearman pair are the other. Not a certificate.
His first son, James, is baptised at Weston
Father Joseph, a labourer; mother Sarah. Probably named for Sarah's brother, the lodger of the census.
As Caroline Wallis, daughter of Joseph, a labourer, and Sarah, at Weston.
In Maiden Street, Weston, with nine children
Indexed Wallace in 1871 and Wallis in 1881; a straw-plaiting household. The 1871 index puts his birth in 1829, two years after the baptism. A family called Field lodged with them in 1881.
At Hitchin, vol 3a p729. One Joseph Wallis of that age in the district between 1881 and 1915; a Joseph Wallis who died in 1900 was an infant, and is not him.
gaps: No certificate has been read. His marriage certificate of 1851 would name his father and Sarah's, and his death certificate his age and the informant.
His father's death, and his grandparents, are on his father's page; every rung there is a register or an index entry and none is a certificate.

people.name: Sarah Field
people.why: Her baptism, her marriage and her death are register and index entries matched by name, parish and age; her brother's lodging in her house in 1851 makes the match to her baptism as firm as a name can. Her age at death is two years younger than the baptism.
people.dek: The daughter of a Weston labourer, married at 21 to a man whose own sister and mother lived in the same village.

parents.mark: probable, with a doubt about which William

facts: William Field, bachelor, and Elizabeth Phillips, spinster, both of Weston Holy Trinity; witnesses James Wallis and Mary Warren. A James Wallis stood witness at this wedding, which is the first sign of the two families knowing each other.
See Joseph Wallis's page: his father and her mother were first cousins, through Ann Phillips and her brother James.

Sarah, daughter of William and Elizabeth Field, a labourer, at Weston Holy Trinity. Her brothers and sisters baptised there to the same parents are Emma (23 May 1824), James (25 Feb 1827) and Charlotte (4 Nov 1832); every Field baptism at Weston in FreeREG for 1824 to 1833 was read, eight in all.
A labourer's wife of 21, with her brother lodging

Sarah Wallis, wife, born at Weston, in her husband's house with James Field, a lodger of 24, an agricultural labourer also born at Weston (FreeCEN). His age and parish fit the James baptised in 1827 to her parents.
At Hitchin, vol 6 p711 (see his page for the reading of the page).
Mother Sarah, father Joseph, a labourer, at Weston.
At Hitchin, vol 3a p268. Two other Sarah Wallises died in the district in 1885, aged 82 and 84, and are not her.
gaps: No certificate has been read. The marriage certificate of 1851 would give her father's name as written.
A Field family lodged with Joseph and Sarah in 1881 and has not been placed.
Her father's identity among the William Fields is on his page: the baptism of 1802 is the better fit but is not settled.

people.name: William Wallis
people.why: His baptism and his marriage are register entries matched by name and parish, and he is the only William Wallis baptised at Weston between 1790 and 1810; his death is inferred from the 1851 census, in which his wife is a widow.
people.dek: A labourer's son who married at nineteen, fathered at least eight children and died before the census of 1851 left his widow on the parish.

parents.mark: her daughter's middle name says so

facts: Joseph Wallis, bachelor, and Ann Phillips, spinster, both of Weston Holy Trinity; witnesses James Swaine and Robert Hide.

William, son of Joseph and Ann Wallis. His sister Jane was baptised on 2 June 1805 and his sister Esther Philips on 6 May 1810, to the same parents. The second sister's names are the clue to the mother: Esther was the name of Ann Phillips's own mother.

William Wallis, bachelor, and Mary Foster, spinster, both of Weston Holy Trinity, witnesses James Watson and William Kent. He is nineteen, if this is the William baptised in 1807, and the only William Wallis baptised at Weston from 1790 to 1810. His son Joseph is baptised five months later. A Joseph Wallis aged 43, probably his father, is buried at Weston on 6 April 1827, two months after the wedding.
At least seven children baptised at Weston

Joseph (22 Jul 1827), Eliza (6 Nov 1842), Jeremiah (5 Oct 1845) and William (7 May 1848) are in the register to William and Mary Wallis, labourer. Emma, Ann and Hesther are in their mother's household in 1851 and their baptisms were not found.
His widow is on the parish

Mary Wallis, 42, a labourer's widow and a pauper, in Weston village with Emma, Ann, Hesther, Eliza, Jeremiah, William and a granddaughter, Eliza Ann, aged one (HO 107 piece 1709, schedule 81). So William died between the baptism of May 1848 and the census.
gaps: His death has not been found; the index gives no age before 1866 and several William Wallises are possible.

His own parents are one candidate, not a finding. Joseph Wallis and Ann Phillips married at Weston in 1804 and had Jane, William and Esther Philips baptised there; the register names no surname for the mother, and the identification of the William of 1827 with the baptism of 1807 rests on his being the only one.

His father Joseph is most probably the Joseph baptised at Clothall on 5 January 1783 to Joseph and Mary Wallis (who married at Clothall on 26 December 1771), but he was buried at Weston aged 43, which is a year younger than the baptism, and no document names him as the Weston groom of 1804. A Joseph Wallis baptised at Great Munden in 1781 is accounted for as another man: he married a Stains in 1801 and was buried at Great Munden in 1848.

His mother Ann's baptism is the one at Weston on 16 November 1783 to William and Esther Phillips, who married at Weston on 21 February 1775 by licence (William Philips, bachelor, and Esther Wright, spinster, both of Weston; witnesses John Wright and Wm. Hide; the couple and the first witness signed with a cross). A William Phillips, yeoman, was buried at Weston on 20 October 1793, and Esther, widowed, married William Harwood at Weston on 3 October 1795 as Esther Phillips, widow, and is probably the Hester Harwood buried there on 2 October 1831 aged 75 (Esther Wright's baptism is probably that of Hester Wright at Stevenage on 27 December 1754, to John and Sarah Wright; that is a match by forename, date and age and no document names her parents as a Weston bride's). William's own parents are not known: a William Phillips, yeoman, of Weston made a will in 1760 (Hertfordshire Archives, 107HW16 and 16HR150), which has not been read and is the likeliest place to find them. Ann was buried at Weston on 5 April 1833 aged 48, a year younger than the baptism.

people.name: Mary Foster
people.why: Her marriage is a register entry and the baptism at Wallington is matched to the birthplace the 1851 census gives; her age in 1851 is about two years under the baptism and nothing else names her parents.
people.dek: A Wallington girl who married a Weston labourer at twenty, bore at least seven children and was left a pauper widow of forty-four with the youngest still at home.
facts: Thomas Foster and Elizabeth South, at Wallington St Mary. Their first child is baptised in March 1794.
Mary, daughter of Thomas and Elizabeth Foster, the youngest of five baptised there to them: Sarah (16 Mar 1794), Ann (16 Apr 1797), Thomas (30 Jun 1799), Edith (10 Oct 1802) and Mary.
Both of Weston Holy Trinity, she a spinster; witnesses James Watson and William Kent.
A pauper widow of 42, born at Wallington
Mary Wallis, head, in Weston village with six children and a granddaughter. The census gives Wallington as her birthplace and an age two years under the baptism.
gaps: No death or burial after 1851 has been looked for.
Her baptism is matched to her birthplace by the census and to nothing else; no other Mary Foster was baptised at Wallington in the years around 1806.
The baptisms of her parents have not been found: Elizabeth South in particular was not found at Wallington or nearby.

people.name: William Field
people.why: His marriage is a register entry. Which William Field it was is the problem: the baptism of 1802 is the better fit, because a William Field was buried as an infant in March 1798 and the William baptised in 1797 to the same parents may be he, but his age at burial in 1879 fits the baptism of 1797 slightly better than that of 1802.
people.dek: A Weston labourer, the son of a labourer who died when he was about a year old, and the father of the girl who married his wife's cousin's son.

children.mark: a lodger in his sister's house, 1851

facts: Thomas Field and Sarah Wallduck, at Holy Trinity. Their children baptised there: Sarah 1791, Thomas 1793, Mary 1795, William 1797, David 1799 and William 1802.
A William Field is buried as an infant

The William baptised on 19 March 1797 to Thomas and Sarah would be under a year old, and a second William is baptised to the same parents on 24 January 1802, which is what a family usually did when the first had died. The register does not say whose child the infant was.
William, son of Thomas and Sarah Field. His father is buried at Weston on 4 April 1803, a labourer.
Both of Weston Holy Trinity; witnesses James Wallis and Mary Warren. A different William Field, baptised in 1788 to William and Sarah Field of Weston, would have been 35.
Emma (23 May 1824), James (25 Feb 1827), Sarah (12 Jul 1829) and Charlotte (4 Nov 1832), to William and Elizabeth Field, a labourer.
A William Field of Weston is buried aged 80

Which gives a birth in 1798 or 1799. It is two years from the baptism of 1797 and three from that of 1802, so the age is no help in choosing between them, and it is the only William Field of a plausible age buried at Weston after 1832.
gaps: Which William Field it was is not settled. The baptism of 1802 is the better fit if the infant buried in 1798 was the William of 1797, which the register does not say, and the household of William and Elizabeth Field has not been found in the 1851 census in FreeCEN.
His mother Sarah Wallduck belongs to a Wallduck family at Weston that had six children baptised between 1762 and 1777, and she is not one of the six; her own baptism has not been found.
Thomas Field, his father, cannot be told from the other Thomas Fields baptised in Hertfordshire between 1750 and 1775, of whom there are eighteen.

people.name: Elizabeth Phillips
people.why: Her marriage is a register entry and the only Elizabeth Phillips baptised at Weston around 1798, indexed Philips, is the daughter of the Weston couple whose marriage of 1796 is a register entry. Her death has not been found.
people.dek: A Weston girl whose daughter married her own first cousin's son.
facts: Her father is baptised at Weston
James, son of William and Esther Phillips. His sister Ann was baptised there on 16 November 1783, and Ann became the wife of Joseph Wallis.
James Phillips and Sarah Kiddell, Holy Trinity.

Elizabeth, daughter of James and Sarah Philips (so spelt in the index). Her brothers and sisters, baptised there to the same parents, are William (21 Sep 1800), Jane (1803), Sarah (1806), Mary (1808) and James (1812).
Both of Weston; witnesses James Wallis and Mary Warren, so a Wallis stood at the wedding of a Phillips whose aunt had married a Wallis.
Her father is buried at Weston aged 49
James Philips, which fits a birth in 1775 or 1776; her mother, a Sarah Phillips, is buried there on 13 May 1832 aged 56.
gaps: Her death or burial has not been found. An Elizabeth Field buried in the Hitchin workhouse in 1876 aged 83 is five years older than a birth in 1798 and is not claimed.

Her grandparents are William and Esther Phillips, who as William Philips and Esther Wright married by licence at Weston on 21 February 1775; a William Phillips, yeoman, was buried there on 20 October 1793. Esther remarried in 1795 as a widow and is probably the Hester Harwood buried at Weston in 1831 aged 75, and probably the Hester Wright baptised at Stevenage in 1754 to John and Sarah Wright; nothing here says who William's parents were, and John Wright's own parents are two candidates, a John baptised at Stevenage in 1717 to George Wright, a labourer, and Mary Titmus (married 1708), and another in 1719/20 to Robert Wright, a butcher and victualler with a will of 1753, and Mary Hurst (married 1717); Sarah Wright, wife of John, a labourer, was buried at Stevenage in 1770 aged 53, which leans to the labourer's son and settles nothing; if he is, Mary Titmus (born about 1687, buried 1769) is his mother and probably the daughter of William Titmus, yeoman, of Stevenage (a will of 1722, unread) and Mary Harvey (a marriage licence of 1684), which is a candidate and no more; a William Phillips, yeoman, of Weston made a will in 1760 that has not been read.

people.name: William Wear
people.why: He is in two censuses and his son's birth registration; his parents and his marriage are not on the same footing.
people.dek: A sadler in 1851 and a harness maker by 1871, who brought three of his sons up to his own bench in Jamaica Road.
facts: Walworth in 1851, Newington in 1871. Walworth is a district inside Newington parish and is the more precise.

Son of John Wear and Elizabeth, with three siblings baptised the same day. Held as probable: it is a transcribed index and not the register, it gives no occupation, and Newington had a second Wear household.
A marriage that is not proved
A Sarah Bloom married one of four men registered on Stepney vol 2 p430, and one of the four is 'William Weare'. The index does not say which. A certificate would name both fathers.
At Bermondsey (HO107 piece 1560, folio 212), with his wife Sarah and two small sons.
A harness maker in Jamaica Road
Aged 48 (RG10 piece 641, folio 40), with four sons, three of them harness makers at his bench, and a niece of his wife's from Yarmouth.
gaps: His parents are a best candidate, held as probable.
His marriage is not proved.
His death is not established.

people.name: Sarah Bloom
people.why: Her maiden name is from one birth registration and one niece, and her birthplace is disputed between two censuses.
people.dek: Her birthplace is given as Deptford in Kent in 1851 and Bermondsey in Surrey in 1871, which is not a spelling variant.
facts: Born at Deptford, or at Bermondsey
1851 says Deptford, Kent; 1871 says Bermondsey, Surrey. They are different counties.
A marriage that is not proved
A Sarah Bloom married one of four men registered on Stepney vol 2 p430; one of them is 'William Weare'.
Aged 29, wife of William Wear, with two small sons (HO107 piece 1560, folio 212).
Her maiden name is on her son's birth
Robert Wear's birth registration gives the mother's maiden name as Bloom. A married woman's maiden name is never in a census.
A niece from Yarmouth in the house
Sarah Ann Bloom, aged 17, born at Yarmouth, Norfolk (RG10 piece 641). With a Norfolk niece and Norfolk marriages in the index, the Blooms may not be a London family at all.
gaps: Her parents are not known.
Where she was born is not settled.
Her death is not established.

people.name: John Hawkins
people.why: He is in three censuses and a banns entry; his parentage is a best candidate.
people.dek: An agricultural labourer of Aldenham, baptised in 1819, who called the banns for Emma Larkin in 1842 and raised at least eleven children in a hamlet and then at the Red Lion Cottages.
facts: Son of William Hawkins and Mary. He is the only John the register offers in the window, the other Johns being excluded by age. Held as a best candidate: the register cannot show that this child is the Red Lion man.

Most likely the John aged 20 at Aldenham Checkers, in a household of three with Katherine Nicholls and William Kimpton (HO107 piece 438). The 1841 census, which the work list nominated, could not give his parents.
Both resident at Aldenham. What is read is the banns entry; the wedding itself has not been seen.
Head, agricultural labourer, aged 39 (HO107 piece 1714, folio 19), with Emma and four children. The age sits eight years from his 1871 age, and the baptism agrees with 1871.
Aged 51, agricultural labourer, eight in the household, every one of them born in the parish (RG10 piece 1380, folio 10, schedule 58).
gaps: His death is not established.
His parents are a best candidate and not proved.
His age is given as 39 in 1851 and 51 in 1871, which cannot both be right.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Emma Larkin
people.why: Her baptism, her banns and two censuses are records. Her parents are probable: the register names a Robert and a Mary, and only one of two Robert-and-Mary couples at Aldenham can have had her.
people.dek: Carried on this site for weeks as 'Emma Hawkins', which was her married name; she was born Emma Larkin at Aldenham on 3 March 1822.
facts: Baptised on 24 March, daughter of Robert, a labourer, and Mary Larkin; the only Emma Larkin of her generation in the parish, and the birth year matches the 1871 census to the year.
Which Robert and Mary were her parents

There were two couples of that name at Aldenham. Emma was born 272 days after Robert William (4 June 1821), so she cannot share a mother with him, and he is the son of the widow Mary born at Edgware about 1800. That leaves the couple of the 1814 banns, who in 1851 are Robert, 72, and Mary, 69, both born at Aldenham, with daughters Mary and Elizabeth at home. Burials add to it: a Robert Larkin of 45 was buried in September 1832 and a Mary Larkin of 62 in February 1860, fitting the widow and her husband, while Mary of 72 (1855) and Robert of 79 (1859) fit the other pair. This is an argument from birth dates, censuses and burials, and no document names her as their daughter.
Both resident at Aldenham; the banns were called, and the wedding has not been seen.
There was no Emma among the twenty Hawkinses of Aldenham in 1841, which was the clue that she was a Hawkins only by marriage.
gaps: Her parents are probable and not proved: no document names her as the daughter of the couple of the 1814 banns, and the argument rests on one birth interval and the identification of Robert William with the son in the widow's household.
Her death is not established.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: George Castle
people.died: Q4 1885, Hitchin, aged 46 (an index entry matched by name, age and district)
people.why: The 1871 census names him as son-in-law and father; his death is an index entry matched by name, age and district.
people.dek: An agricultural labourer who was widowed within a year and took his baby son to his dead wife's parents.
facts: The 1871 census gives age 30 and Baldock.
Registered at Hitchin. The index puts a Castle and a Giddins on the same page; the 1871 census relationship is what ties them.
George William, registered at Hitchin, within three months of the wedding.
Martha dies, nine to twelve months after the birth. It was not childbirth.
Aged 30, an agricultural labourer, in the house of James and Elizabeth Giddins, with his son George aged 8 (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).

Aged 46, registered at Hitchin, vol 3a p249: the only George Castle death at Hitchin between 1884 and 1886, and the age fits a man born about 1839 to 1840. A tree had said 'died when his son was 23', which agrees. Matched by name, age and district; the certificate has not been read.
gaps: His own parents are not known.
His death certificate has not been read, so the entry above is matched and not proved.

people.name: Martha Giddings
people.why: The 1871 census names her only through the relationships of the people left behind, and that is enough.
people.dek: She is in neither household she belonged to. Her existence is attested by what the 1871 census says about her widower and her son.
facts: Aged about 20 and not in their household at 9 Cottages, Norton End (RG9 piece 816, folio 69), which lists George, John and Emma.
Registered at Hitchin. The index gives a Castle and a Giddins on the same page.
George William, registered at Hitchin. Baptised in January 1863, from a tree.
A Martha Castle death registered at Hitchin, vol 3A p188. A second Martha Castle death in 1865 cannot be ruled out on the index alone, because the death index before 1866 carries no age.
Attested by the people left behind
George Castle, 30, is enumerated as son-in-law in her parents' house and a boy of 8 as grandson. Both relationships run only through her.
gaps: Her death date is the Q3 1863 entry, which cannot be separated from the 1865 one on the index alone.
The register indexes spell her Giddings and the census spells the family Giddins; both are carried here.

people.name: James Giddins
people.why: He is in the 1861 and 1871 censuses at the same address.
people.dek: An agricultural labourer at Norton End who raised a grandson who was not his to raise.
facts: Aged 46, an agricultural labourer born at Baldock, with Elizabeth and the children George 14, John 12 and Emma 6 (RG9 piece 816, folio 69).
At Norton End, a decade on
Aged 57, with his wife, his widowed son-in-law George Castle and a grandson of 8 (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).

This archive wrote that his daughter Emma was born on 7 February 1859. That is Emma Hawkins of Aldenham, a different woman in a different parish; the Emma in this house is Emma Giddins, born about 1855.
gaps: His parents and his marriage have not been looked for in a register. A James Giddings aged 68 was registered at Hitchin in Q1 1883 (vol 3a p257), which fits a man born about 1815, and an Elizabeth Giddings aged 68 in Q2 1883 (vol 3a p250) fits his wife. They are the only James and Elizabeth of that age under any spelling at Hitchin from Q2 1871 to 1895. No record ties them to Norton End, so his death is a candidate and not established.

people.name: Elizabeth Giddins
people.why: She is in the 1861 and 1871 censuses with her husband.
people.dek: Born at Norton, and in 1871 doing platting, the straw-plaiting that kept Hertfordshire women in work for a century.
facts: Aged 46, wife of James Giddins, born at Norton (RG9 piece 816, folio 69).
Aged 57, her occupation straw-plaiting, with a widowed son-in-law and a grandson in the house (RG10 piece 1365, folio 27).
gaps: Her maiden name is not known: she appears under her husband's surname in every record.
Her parents and her marriage are not established. An Elizabeth Giddings aged 68, registered at Hitchin in Q2 1883 (vol 3a p250), fits her death and is not tied to her by any record.

people.name: John Wear
people.why: An index of the Newington baptism register names him as father of four children baptised together, one of whom is William; no record joins him to William beyond that.
people.dek: A Newington man, the best candidate for William Wear's father, who is on this site only as the name on a baptism index.
facts: At Newington, Surrey: Matilda (born 1820), William (1823), Thomas (1825) and Mary Ann (1827). Matilda and Thomas, opened in full, both name John Wear as father and Elizabeth as mother.
Elizabeth (born 1812) and John (born 1817) were baptised together in 1819, in the same parish, with a father named John.
gaps: It is an INDEX of the register and not the register, so it gives no occupation, and the trade is the lever this archive nominated.
Newington had a second Wear household under a John Southey Wear, so a forename match there is not an identification.
His marriage, his trade and his death are not known.

people.name: Elizabeth Wear
people.why: Her name is on two of four transcripts of the baptisms of 10 April 1833, and on no other record.
people.dek: Known only as the mother named on two baptism transcripts at Newington, and held as probable.
facts: Two of the four baptism transcripts, those of Matilda and Thomas, were opened in full and both give the mother as Elizabeth. Mary Ann's was not opened.
gaps: Her maiden name, her birth, her marriage and her death are all unknown.
Which of the Newington children were hers is the same question as whether the household is the right one.

people.name: William Hawkins
people.died: 23 November 1848, buried at Aldenham aged 76 (matched by name and abode)
people.why: The register offers exactly one William-and-Mary pair among 44 Hawkins marriage entries, married in the right year; that is a best candidate and not proof.
people.dek: Called the banns for Mary Appleyard at Aldenham in April 1800; nine children were baptised to a William and Mary Hawkins between 1801 and 1819.
facts: Banns, then marriage, with Mary Appleyard
The banns were read on 20 April 1800 and they were married at Aldenham on 5 May, both of the parish. The marriage entry is now seen.
George 1801, Sarah 1803, Mary 1805, Jane 1808, Thomas 1810, Mary 1812, William 1814, Charlotte 1817 and John 1819, to a William and Mary Hawkins. The reused name Mary suggests the first Mary died.
A widower of 65 at Round Bush

The only William Hawkins at Aldenham old enough to have married in 1800 (HO107 piece 438, book 3, folio 10, page 14, schedule 477), in a household of Mash and Rogers with no wife. His wife Mary had been buried in 1822, which fits. Ages were rounded in 1841, so this is matching and not a find.
Buries a daughter and then his wife

Mary, daughter of William and Mary Hawkins, was buried on 24 April 1820 aged 7, from near the Church; and Mary, wife of William Hawkins, on 30 January 1822 aged 41, from Aldenham Gate. The wife is the Mary Appleyard of 1800 by the husband's name and the order of events.
From near the Church, where his daughter's burial of 1820 also places the family. Matched by name and abode: he is the only William Hawkins of that age at Aldenham in 1841.
gaps: The marriage entry names Mary Appleyard and no parents. His own baptism is a separate gap, below.
His own baptism and parents are unknown.
That the John of 1819 is the Red Lion man is a best candidate.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Mary Appleyard
people.died: 30 January 1822, buried at Aldenham aged 41, as 'wife of William Hawkins' (matched by his name)
people.why: Her maiden name is in the banns and the marriage entry of 1800; her own baptism has not been found.
people.dek: A surname this archive had never held. She married into Aldenham from somewhere her own baptism has not been found.
facts: At Aldenham, both resident. 'Of this parish' in a banns entry is residence at the time and not birth.
At Aldenham, both of the parish; the surname is written Appleyard in the marriage entry as in the banns.
No Appleyard baptism of her generation at Aldenham

All 18 Appleyard baptisms there were read: a John-and-Hannah family ending in 1749 and a William-and-Ann family beginning in 1809, with nothing in between. The register is well covered for those decades, so the absence is real.

Entered as the wife of William Hawkins, from Aldenham Gate, so born about 1780 or 1781. The entry does not give her maiden name; she is identified by her husband's name and the nine children of 1801 to 1819. A daughter Mary had been buried in April 1820, aged 7.
gaps: Her own baptism has not been found. A surname-only search of Hertfordshire Baptisms on Findmypast (16 October 2026) returned 24 Appleyard entries, 21 of them at Aldenham, and no Mary before 1851; a free index finds one Appleyard baptism in Hertfordshire, Middlesex and Buckinghamshire in 1750 to 1800, an Ann at Marylebone, and nine Mary Appleyards in England in 1762 to 1782, every one in Yorkshire. That shows where those indexes find the name and not where she was born. Aldenham holds 21 Appleyard baptisms in that set in all, and none is a Mary.

Her parents and her birthplace are unknown. Of the nine Mary Appleyards baptised in Yorkshire between 1762 and 1782, one was baptised at Kippax on 23 January 1780; that is a coincidence of dates and not a lead.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Robert Larkin
people.died: 20 February 1859, buried at Aldenham aged 79 (matched by name, age and abode)
people.why: The register offers two candidate baptisms; the ages in 1851 and 1859 favour one, and a second Robert accounts for the other.
people.dek: Called the banns for Mary Burch at Aldenham in January 1814. Eleven children were baptised to a Robert and a Mary Larkin between 1814 and 1833, and they cannot all be this couple's.
facts: Banns, then marriage, with Mary Burch

Banns were read on 16 January 1814 and they were married by banns at Aldenham on 6 February, both of the parish, he a bachelor and she a spinster, with Wm Larkins and Wm Nicholls as witnesses. The bride's name is transcribed Barch in the marriage entry. It is the only Robert-and-Mary pair among 30 Larkin marriage entries. Their first child on the register was born on 30 March, 52 days after the wedding.
Eleven children baptised to a Robert and a Mary

Sarah, Mary, Elizabeth, Joseph, Robert William, Emma, Amy, James, John, a second Joseph and Thomas, the father a labourer in every entry. They cannot be one mother's: Emma was born on 3 March 1822, 272 days after Robert William (4 June 1821). A widow Mary Larkin, born at Edgware about 1800, heads a household in 1851 with Robert (30) and Eliza (20), and in 1841 with Robert, Joseph, Eliza and Thomas; she would have been 21 at Robert William's birth. So two Robert-and-Mary couples baptised children at Aldenham. The earlier note here that the first of two Josephs 'had most likely died' is withdrawn: there may be one Joseph in each family.
Two candidate baptisms, and two Roberts

A Robert baptised in 1789 to Robert and Ann would be 62 in 1851 and 70 in 1859, and one baptised in 1781 to James and Sarah would be 70 and 78. The censuses and the burial give 72 and 79, so the age favours 1781. A different Robert Larkin, aged 45, was buried from the Folly on 16 September 1832; he fits the Robert of 1789 and the husband of the widow Mary, and an older Robert, aged 77, was buried from the Alms Houses in 1826. This is matching by age and place, and no document ties either baptism to either man.

Head of a household of five (HO107 piece 1714, folio 13, page 19, schedule 75): Robert Larkin, married, agricultural labourer, born Aldenham; his wife Mary, 69, born Aldenham; daughters Mary Bilby, a widow of 33, and Elizabeth, 31, both laundresses; and a granddaughter Mary Bilby, 6. The daughters match the baptisms of 1815 and 1818 in name and, within about three years, in age. Whether he is the Robert of the 1814 banns is an inference from that match and from the banns being the only Robert-and-Mary marriage in the Aldenham register. Mary Bilby had married William Bilby by banns on 22 October 1843; he was buried on 8 October 1844, aged 29, three months after their daughter Mary was baptised (7 July 1844). That marriage does not name her father.

From the Round Bush Alms Houses. He is matched to this Robert by name, by an age one year off the 1851 census and by an abode that fits an old labourer in the same hamlet as his wife's burial. No document ties the entry to him.
gaps: Which baptism is his is not proved: the ages favour 1781 and nothing ties him to it. He is not in the 1841 index at Aldenham, where the only Robert Larkin is his namesake aged 20 in the widow Mary's household.
The one Robert Larkin burial at Aldenham, on 1 September 1793, carries no age, so it cannot be told whether it is anyone here.
His burial, on 20 February 1859 at Round Bush Alms Houses, is matched and not proved. He is in no later census.
Which of the eleven children are his and Mary Burch's is not settled. Emma is, by the argument on her page; Robert William, the second Joseph and Thomas are marked as probably the other couple's.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers

people.name: Mary Burch
people.died: 14 October 1855, buried at Aldenham aged 72 (matched by name, age and abode)
people.why: Her maiden name rests on one banns entry; her own baptism has not been found.
people.dek: Another surname this archive had never held. She married into Aldenham in 1814 from somewhere her baptism has not been found.
facts: Banns, then marriage, with Robert Larkin

Banns were read on 16 January 1814 and they were married by banns at Aldenham on 6 February, both of the parish, he a bachelor and she a spinster, with Wm Larkins and Wm Nicholls as witnesses. The bride's name is transcribed Barch in the marriage entry. It is the only Robert-and-Mary pair among 30 Larkin marriage entries. Their first child on the register was born on 30 March, 52 days after the wedding.
No Burch baptism of her generation at Aldenham

All 7 Burch baptisms there are of 1811 or later, so none can be hers. The 1851 census says she was born at Aldenham about 1781 or 1782. If that is right her baptism is not under Burch in the Aldenham register, and no Mary Birch was baptised there in the 1770s or 1780s in either free index or Findmypast.

In the household at HO107 piece 1714, folio 13, schedule 75: Mary, born Aldenham, with Robert, 72, and their daughters Mary and Elizabeth. That she is the Mary Burch of the 1814 banns is an inference from the two daughters' baptisms and from the banns being the only Robert-and-Mary marriage at Aldenham.

From Round Bush. A Mary Larkin of that age and hamlet, and the 1851 household was at Round Bush: matched, and the entry does not name a husband. She would be the first of the couple to die, four years before Robert.
gaps: Her own baptism has not been found. A surname-only search of Hertfordshire Baptisms on Findmypast returned 236 Burch entries and no Mary baptised Burch between 1738 and 1856. Her ages (69 in 1851, 72 at burial) put her birth at 1782 or 1783. Two Mary Birch baptisms fit within a year or two: Abbots Langley on 13 January 1782 (father Adam), which fits the census, and Watford, born 27 December 1782 (Charles and Mary), which fits the burial and whose sister Trothy was entered as Burch in 1784. None is chosen. A Burch family was at Aldenham from 1810, and her own parents are not in its registers. Neither candidate is secure: a Mary Birch aged 16 was buried at Abbots Langley in May 1796, who may be the girl of January 1782, and a Mary Birch married James Beech at Watford in February 1804, who may be the Watford girl of December 1782. Either would exclude the candidate, and neither is proved.
Her parents are unknown, and no document says where she was born.
see: Two generations out of the Aldenham registers
